answer.evidence: This is a terrain autotile block, not a standing object. The upper part (rows ~16-47) is a front-facing brick wall with staggered brick courses. It has no top surface and no edge line, only a dark base at about row 47. Below it, rows ~48-112 are a large purple cracked-stone floor, a horizontal surface seen from above, with a dark shadow band at its top edge. The whole tile has a wavy icy/stone border fringe on a dark background. It is a wall-plus-floor composite rather than a single volume with a top and a front face, so it is classed as other.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a 4x3 ground patch with a brick wall band on top and a purple cracked-stone floor below, ringed by a dark spiky border. Visible tones per tile are 6, close to the paving reference at 7 and above the grass reference at 3, so density by that count is acceptable. Near-flat coverage is 38% against 0% for both references, so there are large single-colour areas, mainly the dark border and parts of the floor and brick. The dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline is a neutral near-black line, whereas the references use tinted or textured edges (grass 0%, paving 80%). Shading per material is about 3-4 steps, shallower than the 5-6 of the references. The floor has a repeated scale and crack pattern with a few highlight dots, which gives some texture but little per-stone shading. Overall it reads flatter and more sticker-like than the references, so it fails.
